_doc: Shared-header forms that became byte-proven after functions containing them were already tried. campaign.py next reads this: an unmatched function containing a form's markers ignores every attempt made before `since`, ranks ahead of the regular pool (capped at REOPEN_SHARE of each tier's slots), and its prompt names the form. Marker kinds: `vtable_slot` [offset, value] (a literal pointing at an ro vtable whose word at that offset is value), `words` (literal-pool values), `calls` (bl/b targets), `insn` [mask, value] (instruction encodings). Add an entry whenever a header gains a proven form; remove it once its functions are worked through.

sead-string-tree.hint: uses sead's string classes, now byte-proven in sead_string.h (three-level FixedSafeString tree, SafeString() = cNullChar, cstr/calcLength/copy, FormatFixedSafeString<N>); see the brief's 'String code' construct and docs/LESSONS.md 'sead audit'. Use the header types, never local copies.

sead-list-pushback.hint: pushes onto a sead list: ListImpl::pushBack / OffsetList::pushBack now exist in sead_container.h (thin wrappers over ListNode::insertFront_ 0x0010F1DC); reach the list through a pointer local (see the brief).

sead-wide-string.hint: works on a WIDE (char16/u16) sead string: sead_string.h now has WSafeString / WBufferedSafeString / WFixedSafeString<N> (vtable ro_006F599C, u16 units, the 0x40000 length cap). Use those types, and copyLocal() for a local built over a member array, copy() for a heap/memory destination (they differ in when mStringTop is fetched).

sead-string-append.hint: appends/copies at an offset: BufferedSafeString::append / copyAt now exist in sead_string.h (call them; the out-of-line instance is 0x00689928).

sead-string-copy-ctor.hint: constructs a FixedSafeString<N> FROM a string (SafeString or FixedSafeString): that constructor does NOT clear() first. sead_string.h has FixedSafeString(const SafeString&) / (const FixedSafeString&) now; use them instead of a default ctor plus copy().
